flashcard_questions.q: Which German word, meaning 'dictated peace', did Germans use for the Treaty of Versailles?
How much were German reparations set at?
What percentage of its land did Germany lose under the Treaty?
The Treaty cost Germany 10% of its land and ____ of its population.
What name did nationalists give to the politicians who signed the Treaty?
What was the 'stab in the back' myth?
flashcard_questions.a: The false claim that politicians had betrayed an undefeated German army by surrendering.

flashcard_questions.q: Which harsher treaty had Germany forced on Russia in March 1918?
Why did Clemenceau believe the Treaty had failed France?
flashcard_questions.a: He thought the terms were not harsh enough to guarantee French security.

flashcard_questions.q: What happened to Clemenceau in January 1920?
flashcard_questions.a: He failed to be elected President and resigned at once.

flashcard_questions.q: What did Lloyd George privately predict about the Treaty?
flashcard_questions.a: That another war would have to be fought in 25 years' time.

flashcard_questions.q: Who resigned from the British team and wrote The Economic Consequences of the Peace?
Why did the US Senate refuse to ratify the Treaty?
flashcard_questions.a: Because it did not follow Wilson's Fourteen Points.

flashcard_questions.q: Which country invaded the Ruhr in 1923 after a missed reparations payment?
How much did a loaf of bread cost in Germany in January 1923?
How much did the same loaf cost by November 1923?

notes: 15 cards: 5 term/concept, 4 figure, 3 cause-effect, 2 person, 1 cloze. The two bread-price cards are kept as a matched pair because the contrast is the exam point.
